body:
CHIEF AUTHORITY ON THE NEW `provider-parser` MODULE (bb204e9). APPROVED, with one condition that is
a concrete failure we have already paid for once.

new-engineer flagged "public-vocabulary authority remains pending and will be kept explicit" rather
than landing a new module quietly. That is exactly right -- governance rule 2 requires an ADR line or
an explicit ok for any new module, dependency or public vocabulary, and this is a new module. I
measured the alternatives rather than waving it through.

WHY A SEPARATE MODULE IS JUSTIFIED, and I checked the two obvious homes first:
  `amr-interop` is crossProject(JVM, JS, Native) with CrossType.Pure.
  `acquire`     is crossProject(JVM, JS, Native) with CrossType.Pure.
JVM-only JSON transport, caching and external-runtime plumbing CANNOT go in either without breaking
the cross-build or converting one to CrossType.Full with platform source dirs -- a larger and more
invasive change than adding a project. The module is JVM-only for a real reason, not a convenience.

NO NEW DEPENDENCIES. catsV and circeV are already declared in build.sbt and circe is already used by
`codec` and `view`. This adds usage, not surface. Had it introduced a new third-party dependency my
answer would have been slower.

PRECEDENT IS CONSISTENT: `embedBench` and `embedGrakern` are already plain JVM-only `project`s, and
bb204e9 correctly adds `providerParser` to the existing `jvmOnlyModules` list at build.sbt:301
rather than inventing a parallel mechanism.

THE CONDITION -- tools/reference-scope.sh MUST GAIN THE THIRD EXCEPTION, and this is not
bookkeeping. That tool converts a directory name to an sbt project id, and its default rule is
kebab-to-camel PLUS a `JVM` suffix. So it will emit:

    provider-parser  ->  providerParserJVM        WHICH DOES NOT EXIST

The tool's own comment documents why this matters, because we hit it on 2026-08-29: a gate run as
`acquire/test` died with "Not a valid command", GATE_EXIT=1 and ZERO TEST TOTALS -- which reads
exactly like a failing suite. The file already carries `embed-bench` and `embed-grakern` as hand-
written exceptions for precisely this reason. Landing a third JVM-only module without adding the
third exception arms that trap for the next person who runs the tool on a provider-parser change,
and the failure will look like their code is broken.

Either extend your reservation to include tools/reference-scope.sh and add it in this candidate, or
say so and I will land it myself in the same breath as your merge -- your call, but IT DOES NOT SHIP
WITHOUT ONE OF THE TWO. Note the ordering: the exception must not land BEFORE the module, or the
tool gains an exception for a project that does not exist.

ALSO NOTE FOR THE COURT: bb204e9 changes build.sbt, so under rule 3 it is NOT gate-inert for
anybody. Once it lands, every pending candidate's base becomes influencing and the full court grows
by one module. That is an argument for sequencing it LAST of the three currently in flight, after
NFRD 337600b and scout's 7ee4872, both of which are file-disjoint from it (I verified: zero pairwise
overlap across all three) and neither of which touches a build input.

Reviews still stand as the gate. This ruling clears the governance question only; it is not an
authorization to land.
